name: Sydney Kamlager-Dove

statements.quote: The 15% fee that Trump is planning to charge NVIDIA and AMD to sell AI chips to China is explicitly outlawed in the Export Controls Reform Act, and for good reason. It would turn export control licenses into pay-to-play arrangements that allow Trump to sideline national security considerations and extort U.S. companies.
statements.venue: Press release with opening remarks, House Foreign Affairs South and Central Asia Subcommittee hearing on export controls

statements.quote: Trump is doing all of this while pursuing counterproductive immigration policies like the $100,000 fee for H-1B visas that is driving away high-skilled talent that we need to win the AI race.
statements.venue: Press release with opening remarks, House Foreign Affairs South and Central Asia Subcommittee hearing on export controls

statements.quote: Trump rescinded the AI diffusion rule on the same day he arrived in the Middle East to announce unprecedented sales of AI chips to the UAE and Saudi Arabia before any security agreements were put in place.
statements.venue: Press release with opening remarks, House Foreign Affairs South and Central Asia Subcommittee hearing on export controls

statements.quote: And I think that agreement that was made yesterday, I think that dinner that happened yesterday should have everyone's eyes wide open about the five-alarm fire that we could potentially be grappling with with the revenue schemes and the profit selling questionable schemes of these chips.
statements.venue: House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing transcript, 'Export Control Loopholes: Chipmaking Tools and Their Subcomponents'

statements.quote: The U.S. intelligence community has raised concerns about G42's interest in accessing advanced U.S. AI chips, citing the risk that such technologies could be diverted for PRC military or intelligence use. Despite these security concerns, the Trump Administration decided to sell chips directly to G42 only after Sheikh Tahnoon entered into very high-value business deals with President Trump.
statements.venue: Press release quoting joint letter to Commerce Department Inspector General

raw:
I found five statements in her own words, all on AI chips, export controls and national security. I couldn't find usable text for the ABC News interview, the Helen Toner hearing questioning, the Forbes/YouTube clip or the BIN interview on AI and creative jobs. Only summaries of those turned up, so I left them out.

Two caveats on the statements:
- The UAE chip letter was co-signed by other lawmakers, so the quote is joint wording.
- I judged these AI-related because they concern AI chips, the AI race and export controls. None is a broad statement about AI itself.
